newsitem.title: GERMANY: Thyssen Industrie stable in quarter.
newsitem.headline: Thyssen Industrie stable in quarter.

text.p: Thyssen Industrie AG said its sales and orders were little changed in the first quarter of 1996/97 from the year-earlier quarter.
In the quarter to December, sales totalled 1.9 billion marks ($1.1 billion), while orders were 2.2 billion marks, chairman Eckhard Rohkamm told the annual shareholders' meeting.
The Thyssen AG unit is implementing its restructuring programme, but sees risks ahead this year, including sluggish markets for automobiles and freighters.
Government plans to eliminate depreciation allowances for freighters, if implemented, would force Thyssen to make additional cost cuts, Rohkamm said.
He repeated that Thyssen is committed to the Transrapid high-speed rail project, but not at any price.
A new cost study on the project expected by early April should provide the basis for a solution acceptable to the government, Deutsche Bahn and the private partners, he said.
-- Terence Gallagher, Bonn newsroom, 49-228-26097150 ($ = 1.715 German Marks)
